data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by an abnormally slow image pull process. The 53 MB image took 56.488 seconds to download, resulting in a throughput of approximately 0.9 MB/s, which is significantly below the expected performance threshold of 5 MB/s. No other phases, such as scheduling or application initialisation, contributed to the SLO breach.

findings.statement: The image pull phase lasted 56.488 seconds for a 53 MB image.
The pull throughput was approximately 0.9 MB/s (944,075 bytes/s), which is well below the 5 MB/s performance baseline.

ruled_out.reason: The image size is only 53 MB, which is not large enough to justify a 56-second pull time under normal network conditions.
The scheduling phase duration was 0.0 seconds, indicating no delay in pod placement.
Application initialisation took only 0.909 seconds, which is negligible compared to the total startup time.

recommendations.rationale: Pre-pulling the image ensures it is already present on nodes before the pod is scheduled, mitigating registry throughput bottlenecks.
The low throughput suggests potential issues with registry load, rate limiting, or the lack of a local pull-through cache.
